purpose: Compile a declared intention into a verified declarative task and reversible sensory representation plan.

activities.label: compile semantic intent, declarative machine and representation plan
mutate analogy, transitions and sensory controls to verify blocking

queries.expression: does a declared intention compile to a state machine and representation plan without executing generated code
does an independent oracle reject a mutated transition or unexplained event
does the representation layer remain bounded, reversible and driven only by declared interaction signals

assumptions: The fixture is a synthetic semantic example, not a game reverse-engineering claim.
A declarative intermediate representation is safer to inspect than direct arbitrary source execution.
Tempo, motion and attention weight are rendering parameters, not measurements of a person's nervous system.
Declared interaction signals do not establish emotion, impairment or diagnosis.
kill_tests: Missing residue on a non-equivalent mapping blocks compilation.
A mutated transition must disagree with the independent oracle.
A representation plan without preview, accept or revert is rejected.
Periodic flashing and implicit friction inference are rejected.
Unknown events return unavailable or blocked rather than inventing a transition.
No human data, camera, network or generated-code execution is allowed.
unknowns: Whether a person learns or builds faster with the contrastive map.
Whether a declared tempo or reduced-motion policy feels better in sustained work.
Whether an agent can infer a useful semantic map from real documentation without introducing unsupported relations.
Whether the declarative machine is sufficient for a real application adapter.
Which open-source parser or UI catalog should be adopted in a later runtime.
